---
title: "1 · Introduction to machine learning in marine science"
description: "What machine learning is, how it differs from statistical modelling, and when prediction is not the same as understanding."
categories: [foundations]
---

Most marine scientists already fit models. You have written a GLM, checked residuals,
looked at a p-value, and drawn a conclusion about how temperature affects abundance.
So the obvious question about machine learning is: what is different?

The short answer is *what the model is for*. A statistical model is usually built to
tell you something about the world — the size of an effect, whether it is
distinguishable from noise. A machine-learning model is usually built to make good
predictions about cases it has not seen. Those two goals pull in different directions,
and a model that excels at one can be useless at the other.

This section sets up that distinction and the vocabulary the rest of the course uses.

## In this section

- What machine learning is, and how it differs from traditional statistical modelling
- Examples of machine-learning applications in marine science
- The main types of learning: supervised, unsupervised, and neural-network-based
- Prediction versus explanation, and what each can support scientifically
